items.title: Introduction
items.text:
Welcome to AI-VERDE, an open source platform that facilitates access to commercial and on-premise LLMs with budget and access controls. AI-VERDE stands for "AI Virtual Explorer for Research, Discovery, and Education". There are two pieces to AI-VERDE, the AI-VERDE chat interface and the AI-VERDE API (application programming interface).

Our chat interface provides you with an interactive, AI-powered assistant designed to enhance your learning, research, and teaching experiences. Using language models from commercial providers and CyVerse's on-premise infrastructure, this interface allows you to engage with an advanced AI assistant capable of answering questions, offering explanations, and assisting with various tasks in real time.

items.title: Key Features
items.text:
• Interactive Q&A: Simply type your question, and the assistant will provide clear, concise answers on a wide range of topics.
  • Designed for small teams and courses: Use AI-VERDE for small teams, labs, and courses.
  • Bring Your Own (BYO) LLM: Instructors and team leads can optionally bring their own commercial or third-party LLM to AI-VERDE or use CyVerse's on-premise LLMs.
  • Built for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Instructors and team leads can optionally configure AI-VERDE to provide answers strictly from source documents.
  • Budget management and cost savings: If you're using commercial services, tokens cost money. Use AI-VERDE to control model access, with budgets for each course or team and per individual (budgets are set by CyVerse on request).
  • Built-in Guardrails: Ensure the responsible, safe, and effective use of AI-VERDE within your team and course.

items.title: Getting Started with AI-VERDE Chat
items.text: This guide will help you get up and running quickly, so you can start making the most out of your experience with our AI-VERDE Chat.

items.title: 1. Sign In
items.text:
Before using the AI-VERDE chat interface, ensure you are signed in with your institution's credentials.

Note

AI-VERDE is currently only available to the University of Arizona community.

  1. Go to https://chat.cyverse.ai/.
  2. Click the Sign In button. You will be taken to CILogon.
  3. On CILogon, select your identity provider. For University of Arizona users, select The University of Arizona.
  4. Click the Log On button.
  5. Log in with your institution’s login process (for University of Arizona users, your NetID).
  6. You will be returned to AI-VERDE, signed in.

items.title: 2. Select Your Team or Course
items.text: Once signed in, find your course or team card and click on the chat button.

items.title: 3. Ask Your First Question
items.text:
After clicking on the course or team card, the page will show a text box where you can interact with AI-VERDE. You can then:

  • Type a question directly in the chat box (e.g., "Why is the sky blue?").
  • Press Send to submit.
  • Receive a Response within seconds, tailored to your query.

items.title: 4. Continue the Conversation
items.text: You can ask follow-up questions for further clarification, request examples, or explore related topics.

items.title: Example:
items.text:
1. Initial Question: "Explain the concept of ecosystems in biology."
  2. Follow-Up: "Can you provide examples of different types of ecosystems?"
  3. Further Detail: "How does biodiversity impact ecosystem stability?"

items.title: Tips for Using the Chat Interface
items.text:
• Be Specific: Detailed questions yield the best responses.
  • Explore Broadly: If your team or course is not targeting specific documents, you can ask about a wide range of topics or request explanations for academic concepts.
  • Engage in Multi-Step Conversations: If you need deeper insights, use follow-up questions to refine the responses.

items.title: Usage Budgets
items.text: Each course or team has a usage budget, and some courses also set a budget for each student. By default, budgets are monthly and reset on the 1st of each month. Some courses use a different reset schedule. If you reach your budget, you can use AI-VERDE again once it resets. Ask your instructor or team lead if you're unsure which schedule applies.

items.title: Introduction to AI-VERDE API
items.text: AI-VERDE exposes an OpenAI-compatible API, so any tool or library that supports OpenAI can connect to it using your AI-VERDE API key. AI-VERDE also accepts Anthropic-style requests (used by Claude Code and the Anthropic SDK) and, for Claude Code only, AWS Bedrock-style requests for Claude models hosted on AWS Bedrock. This section explains how to get your key and use it across a range of environments.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
Before using the API you will need to:

  1. Obtain your API key — Sign in at chat.cyverse.ai, open your course or team details, and copy the key from the API Key tab. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key for step-by-step instructions.
  2. Know which models are available — Your available models are listed on the same API Key page. You can also retrieve them programmatically; see Getting a List of Models.

items.title: What's in This Section
items.text: Section What it covers Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models Claude models on AWS Bedrock with Claude Code and the Claude Code for VS Code extension Using Your API Key in Code Python integration with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and the Anthropic Python SDK Using CLI Coding Assistants Terminal-based AI coding tools: Claude Code Router, Aider, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode Using IDEs Editor integration for VSCode Using Desktop Clients GUI chat clients such as ChatboxAI

items.title: Base URL and Authentication
items.text:
When configuring a client, you need your API key (copied from the AI-VERDE dashboard) and a base URL. The base URL depends on which style of API the client speaks:

API style Base URL Used by OpenAI-compatible https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 Aider, Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code Router, ChatboxAI, VSCode, and most OpenAI clients Anthropic-style https://llm-api.cyverse.ai Claude Code (Anthropic models), Claude Code (non-Anthropic models), Anthropic Python SDK AWS Bedrock https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock Claude Code on Bedrock, Claude Code for VS Code on Bedrock

If your course details show a different base URL ending in /v1, use it for OpenAI-compatible clients, remove /v1 for Anthropic-style clients, and replace /v1 with /bedrock for AWS Bedrock.

Note

The LangChain and LlamaIndex examples use LiteLLM's litellm_proxy provider, which takes the base URL without /v1 (https://llm-api.cyverse.ai).

OpenAI-compatible clients send the API key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>), and Anthropic-style clients may send it in an x-api-key header instead; AI-VERDE accepts either. Each guide shows which setting or environment variable holds the key for that tool.

items.title: Aider
items.text: You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API Key with Aider, self-described "AI pair programming in your terminal". More information on installing and using Aider can be found here, https://aider.chat.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API Key. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key.
  2. Note the model(s) you want to configure for Aider. See Getting a List of Models.
  3. Install Aider. Instructions can be found here, https://aider.chat/#getting-started.
  4. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal on a Linux system with Aider.

items.title: 1. Configuring Aider
items.text:
1. Create a $HOME/.aider.conf.yml file with the following contents:

    openai-api-key: insert-your-aiverde-api-key
openai-api-base: https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1
model: openai/insert-default-model

  2. Replace insert-your-aiverde-api-key with your AI-VERDE API Key.

  3. Replace the text insert-default-model with the AI-VERDE model. For example, to use gemma-4-26b-it, the model field would be set to openai/gemma-4-26b-it. If the model name already contains a provider prefix (e.g. nrp/<model>), keep it and add openai/ in front (e.g. openai/nrp/<model>).

Note

This is the minimal configuration needed to use Aider. If you want to set other configuration for any models, you can add a $HOME/.aider.model.metadata.json file. Instructions on the configuration values that can be set in this file can be found here, https://aider.chat/docs/config/adv-model-settings.html.

items.title: 2. Running Aider
items.text:
Run Aider with the following command:

aider

Note

You may get additional prompts if you're not in a git repo and if you have not configured your model further (see note above). You can also run aider with aider --no-show-model-warnings if you prefer to ignore model warnings.

If you are successful entering Aider, congratulations!

items.title: Claude Code (using non-Anthropic Models)
items.text:
You can follow these instructions to use your VERDE API Key after installing Claude Code. More information on using Claude Code can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview.

Note

These instructions assume you are using a space that is connected to non-Anthropic models. Even though Claude Code is using non-Anthropic models, the API it uses is still Anthropic-style; the API is translated by Verde's LiteLLM into OpenAI-compatible or other supported formats.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Your VERDE course or team must have access to at least one non-Anthropic model. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  2. Obtain your VERDE API Key. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Note the model name(s) you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here.
  4. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  5. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal on a system with Claude Code and bash installed.

items.title: 1. Configure Claude Code
items.text: You can use the same model for all tiers (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) or you can use different models for each tier. The model names must match the exact model name in LiteLLM, as returned by your model list.

items.title: Option 1: ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended)
items.text:
Add the following env section to ~/.claude/settings.json (create the file if it does not exist). Settings in this file apply every time you run Claude Code, in any terminal.

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<model name for opus-tier model>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<model name for sonnet-tier model>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<model name for haiku-tier model>",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "<model name for primary model>"
  }
}

For example:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "gpt-oss-120b",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "gemma-4-26b-it",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "gemma-4-26b-it",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "gpt-oss-120b"
  }
}

If the file already has other settings, add the env section alongside them rather than replacing the file.

items.title: Option 2: Shell environment variables
items.text:
Alternatively, export the same variables in your terminal before launching Claude Code:

export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="<model name for opus-tier model>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="<model name for sonnet-tier model>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="<model name for haiku-tier model>"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="<model name for primary model>"

Exported variables only last for the current terminal session. To avoid re-entering them each session, add the lines to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic Base URL, simply remove /v1 (e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 => https://llm-api.cyverse.ai). If both ~/.claude/settings.json and your shell set the same variable, the value in ~/.claude/settings.json is used.

items.title: 2. Start Claude Code
items.text:
You can then run Claude Code.

claude

The first time Claude Code detects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, it asks whether to use the custom API key. Select Yes. You can run /status inside Claude Code to confirm the base URL and API key it is using.

items.title: If you need to change your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your VERDE API Key, update ANTHROPIC_API_KEY wherever you set it in step 1 (~/.claude/settings.json or your shell profile), then restart Claude Code. If you previously declined the key prompt, Claude Code ignores the key without asking again; re-enable it with the Use custom API key option under /config.

items.title: Claude Code (using Anthropic Models)
items.text:
You can follow these instructions to use your VERDE API Key after installing Claude Code. More information on using Claude Code can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview.

Note

These instructions assume you are using a space that is connected to Anthropic models (Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku from Anthropic, Azure or other providers with Anthropic-style APIs). If you need access to Claude Code using a non-Anthropic model, then see the instructions here or use Claude Code Router.

Note

If your model is hosted on AWS Bedrock, then see the instructions here. The Bedrock setup uses ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN instead of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, because Claude Code only sends ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN when talking to a Bedrock endpoint.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Your VERDE course or team must be configured to use Anthropic models (see instructor or team lead).
  2. Obtain your VERDE API Key. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Note the model names for the Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models available to your course or team. Instructions for listing available models can be found here.
  4. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  5. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal on a system with Claude Code and bash installed.

items.title: 1. Configure Claude Code
items.text: Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6 or my-team/claude-sonnet-4-6). Use the exact names from your model list; Anthropic's public model IDs (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6) will not work.

items.title: Option 1: ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended)
items.text:
Add the following env section to ~/.claude/settings.json (create the file if it does not exist). Settings in this file apply every time you run Claude Code, in any terminal.

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<model name for opus>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<model name for sonnet>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<model name for haiku>"
  }
}

For example:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "my-team-claude-opus-4-6",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"
  }
}

If the file already has other settings, add the env section alongside them rather than replacing the file.

items.title: Option 2: Shell environment variables
items.text:
Alternatively, export the same variables in your terminal before launching Claude Code:

export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="<model name for opus>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="<model name for sonnet>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="<model name for haiku>"

Exported variables only last for the current terminal session. To avoid re-entering them each session, add the lines to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic Base URL, simply remove /v1 (e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 => https://llm-api.cyverse.ai). If both ~/.claude/settings.json and your shell set the same variable, the value in ~/.claude/settings.json is used.

items.title: 2. Start Claude Code
items.text:
You can then run Claude Code.

claude

The first time Claude Code detects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, it asks whether to use the custom API key. Select Yes. You can run /status inside Claude Code to confirm the base URL and API key it is using.

items.title: If you need to change your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your VERDE API Key, update ANTHROPIC_API_KEY wherever you set it in step 1 (~/.claude/settings.json or your shell profile), then restart Claude Code. If you previously declined the key prompt, Claude Code ignores the key without asking again; re-enable it with the Use custom API key option under /config.

items.title: Codex
items.text: You can follow these instructions to use your VERDE API Key after installing Codex. More information on using Codex can be found here, https://github.com/openai/codex.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your VERDE API Key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  3. Install Codex. Instructions can be found here, https://github.com/openai/codex.
  4. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal on a system with Codex and bash installed.

items.title: 1. Setup the Codex configuration file
items.text:
Codex saves its configuration at ~/.codex/config.toml. Add the following content to the configuration file (replace lines in existing content where appropriate), replacing <your-model-name> with the model you'd like to use.

model = "<your-model-name>"
model_provider = "verde"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium" # change this if you want to adjust the reasoning effort for the model
approvals_reviewer = "user" # change this if you want to adjust the reviewer for approvals, the other option is "auto_review"

[model_providers.verde]
name = "verde"
base_url = "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1"
env_key = "VERDE_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
stream_idle_timeout_ms = 7200000
stream_max_retries = 5
request_max_retries = 4

For example, your existing ~/.codex/config.toml file may look like this:

model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "high"
approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"

[projects."/home/my_user/my_git_repo_1"]
trust_level = "trusted"

[projects."/home/my_user/my_git_repo_2"]
trust_level = "trusted"

[notice.model_migrations]
"gpt-5.3-codex" = "gpt-5.4"
"gpt-5.4" = "gpt-5.5"

[tui.model_availability_nux]
"gpt-5.5" = 4
"gpt-5.6-sol" = 1
After the update, your ~/.codex/config.toml file should look like this:

model = "gpt-oss-120b"
model_provider = "verde"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium"
approvals_reviewer = "user"

[model_providers.verde]
name = "verde"
base_url = "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1"
env_key = "VERDE_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
stream_idle_timeout_ms = 7200000
stream_max_retries = 5
request_max_retries = 4

[projects."/home/my_user/my_git_repo_1"]
trust_level = "trusted"

[projects."/home/my_user/my_git_repo_2"]
trust_level = "trusted"

[notice.model_migrations]
"gpt-5.3-codex" = "gpt-5.4"
"gpt-5.4" = "gpt-5.5"

[tui.model_availability_nux]
"gpt-5.5" = 4
"gpt-5.6-sol" = 1

Export the following environment variable before launching Codex (replacing <your-ai-verde-api-key> with your VERDE API Key).

export VERDE_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"

To avoid re-entering this each session, add the line to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc). Then, you can source your shell profile.

items.title: 2. Start Codex
items.text:
You can then run Codex.

codex

items.title: If you need to change your VERDE_API_KEY
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your VERDE API Key, simply re-set the VERDE_API_KEY environment variable, then restart Codex.

items.title: Using your AI-VERDE API key to integrate with LangChain
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 1. Install LangChain python libraries
items.text: pip install langchain-litellm
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 2. Obtain variables to integrate AI-VERDE with LangChain
items.text:
See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key for instructions.

You can obtain a list of the models you have access to with the following command; denoted by "id":

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer [AI-VERDE API KEY]" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 3. Create python scripts
items.text:
from langchain_litellm import ChatLiteLLM

llm = ChatLiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_key="[AI-VERDE API KEY]",
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai")

print(llm.invoke("Hello, world!"))

Alternatively, you can include the API key as an environment variable or secret to avoid storing it in plain text:

import getpass
import os

if not os.environ.get("AIVERDE_API_KEY"):
  os.environ["AIVERDE_API_KEY"] = getpass.getpass("Enter AI-VERDE API key: ")
api_key = os.environ["AIVERDE_API_KEY"]

from langchain_litellm import ChatLiteLLM

llm = ChatLiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_key=api_key,
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai")

print(llm.invoke("Hello, world!"))
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.text: pip install llama-index-core llama-index-llms-litellm
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 2. Obtain variables to integrate AI-VERDE with LlamaIndex
items.text:
See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key for instructions.

You can obtain a list of the models you have access to with the following command; denoted by "id":

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer [AI-VERDE API KEY]" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 3. Write python scripts
items.text:
from llama_index.llms.litellm import LiteLLM
from llama_index.core.llms import ChatMessage

llm = LiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    api_key="[AI-VERDE API KEY]",)

message = ChatMessage(role="user", content="Hey! how's it going?")
response = llm.chat([message])

print(response)

Alternatively, you can include the API key as an environment variable or secret to avoid storing it in plain text:

import getpass
import os

if not os.environ.get("AIVERDE_API_KEY"):
  os.environ["AIVERDE_API_KEY"] = getpass.getpass("Enter AI-VERDE API key: ")
api_key = os.environ["AIVERDE_API_KEY"]

from llama_index.llms.litellm import LiteLLM
from llama_index.core.llms import ChatMessage

llm = LiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    api_key=api_key,)

message = ChatMessage(role="user", content="Hey! how's it going?")
response = llm.chat([message])

print(response)

Note

LlamaIndex embedding support is outlined here, but functionality depends on access to an embedding model through AI-VERDE.

items.title: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS
items.text:
This tutorial explains how to store your AI-VERDE API key in environment variables on macOS, so that command-line tools and scripts can use it without you pasting it each time.

Most OpenAI-compatible tools read two environment variables:

  • OPENAI_API_KEY: your AI-VERDE API key
  • OPENAI_BASE_URL: the AI-VERDE API base URL, https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1

See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key if you do not have your key yet.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Step 1: Open Terminal
items.text:
1. Launch the Terminal application on your Mac:

    • Use Command + Space to open Spotlight.
    • Type Terminal and press Enter.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Step 2: Determine Your Shell
items.text:
Check which shell you’re using by running:

echo $SHELL
  • If the output is /bin/zsh (the default on macOS), your configuration file is ~/.zshrc.
  • If the output is /bin/bash, your configuration file is ~/.bash_profile.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Step 3: Add the Variables to Your Shell Profile
items.text:
1. Open your configuration file in a text editor:

    nano ~/.zshrc

    (For bash, use nano ~/.bash_profile instead.)

  2. Add the following lines at the end of the file, replacing your_api_key_here with your AI-VERDE API key. Keep the quotes, and do not put spaces around the =.

    export OPENAI_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1"

  3. Save and exit: press Ctrl + O to save, Enter to confirm, then Ctrl + X to exit nano.

  4. Apply the changes to your current terminal:

    source ~/.zshrc

    (For bash, use source ~/.bash_profile instead.) New terminal windows will pick up the variables automatically.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Step 4: Verify the Variables
items.text:
Confirm the variables are set:

echo $OPENAI_BASE_URL
echo $OPENAI_API_KEY

The terminal should display the base URL and your API key.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Step 5: Test the Key with a cURL Request
items.text:
List the models available to your API key:

curl -s "$OPENAI_BASE_URL/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY"

A JSON response containing a "data" list of models means your key works. See Getting a List of Models for ways to format the output.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Step 6: Secure Your Key
items.text:
1. Avoid hardcoding keys in scripts; read them from environment variables instead.
  2. Use .env files with tools like dotenv for larger projects, and do not commit them to version control.
  3. If your key is compromised, contact your instructor or team lead to have it regenerated.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Variable is empty: Make sure you ran source on the correct configuration file, or open a new terminal window.
  • Variable is empty in a new terminal: Check that you edited the configuration file for your shell (Step 2).
  • 401 or authentication error from curl: Check that the key was copied completely and that there are no extra spaces inside the quotes.
  • Permission denied: Check the file permissions of your shell profile.

You're all set! You can now use your API key securely on macOS.
path: Step-by-Step Guide: Using an API Key on macOS

items.title: Getting a List of Models
items.text:
There are three ways to obtain a list of models:

  1. Go to this page to view the list of CyVerse models. This list does not include models from external inference services e.g., Jetstream2.
  2. Viewing your models in the Course Details.
  3. Using your API Key to view your models.

items.title: Viewing your models in the Course Details
items.text:
Your available models will be visible in the AI-VERDE application. These are the steps:

  1. Go to https://chat.cyverse.ai.
  2. After successfully logging in, click the Details button of your course.
  3. Click the "API Key" tab.
  4. The "Available Models" section lists all the models your course has access to.

items.title: Using your API Key to view your models
items.text:
After obtaining your API Key from your course/team, you can obtain a detailed list of available models using curl:

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Alternatively, you can use jq or python's json module to view the output in a more human readable format.

Option 1: If you have jq installed:

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'|jq

Option 2: If you have Python installed (json.tool is part of the standard library):

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" |python -m json.tool

items.title: OpenCode
items.text: OpenCode is an open-source command-line interface (CLI) for interacting with large language models (LLMs). It provides a simple and flexible way to use LLMs for various tasks, such as text generation, code completion, and more.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your VERDE API Key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name(s) you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  3. Install OpenCode. Instructions can be found here, https://opencode.ai/.
  4. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal on a system with OpenCode and bash installed.

items.title: 1. Set up the OpenCode configuration file
items.text:
OpenCode uses a configuration file to define custom providers and models. The configuration file is located at either of the following locations:

  • (Mac/Linux) ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
  • (Mac/Linux) ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc (jsonc is a superset of json that allows comments)

Here is an example configuration file for OpenCode that uses the AI-VERDE provider and models:

{
  "provider": {
    "litellm": { // this is the identifier for the provider, you can choose any name you like, it needs to be unique in the provider list
      "name": "AI-Verde", // this is the display name of the provider (what is shown by the `/model` command), you can choose any name you like
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", // this is the npm package that provides the provider's API, use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` unless you know what you are doing
      "models": {
        "gpt-oss-120b": { // this is the model name shown in AI-Verde
            "name": "my-gpt-oss-120b" // this is the display name of the model (what is shown by the `/model` command), you can choose any name you like
        },
        "gemma-4-26b-it": {
            "name": "my-gemma-4-26b-it"
        }
      },
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", // replace this with your AI-VERDE API Key
        "baseURL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1", // this is the base URL for AI-VERDE, copy-paste from the same page where you got your API Key
        "timeout": 600000 // optional, this is the timeout in milliseconds for API requests, default is 600000 (10 minutes)
      }
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"
}

items.title: 2. Start OpenCode
items.text:
You can then run OpenCode.

opencode

Use /model command to select the model you want to use. You can also use /model <model-name> to switch models on the fly.

items.title: If you need to change your API Key
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your VERDE API Key, you can simply replace your api key in the configuration file in step 1.

items.title: Examples of using your AI-VERDE API Key in VSCode
OpenAI

Note

Check if you have access to an OpenAI model by running the following command and looking for OpenAI model IDs (e.g. gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini). These IDs correspond to the model name.

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer [AI-VERDE API KEY]" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq

items.title: Using AI-VERDE with AWS Bedrock
items.text:
AWS Bedrock is Amazon's fully managed service for accessing foundation models from leading AI providers. AI-VERDE allows users to use AWS Bedrock-provided Anthropic Claude models with Claude Code, both in the terminal and in the VS Code extension.

Note

Currently, the subsequent instructions focus on using Anthropic Claude models from AWS Bedrock. As other models are provided, the instructions will be updated.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Before connecting Claude Code to AI-VERDE, you will need:

  • An AI-VERDE API key — sign in at chat.cyverse.ai, open your course or team details, and copy the key from the API Key tab. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key for step-by-step instructions.
  • The AI-VERDE Bedrock base URL: https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock (or the URL shown in your course details, with /v1 replaced by /bedrock).
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
AI-VERDE acts as a proxy between your application and the underlying model. When you send a request to the AI-VERDE endpoint, AI-VERDE authenticates it against your team or course budget, applies any configured guardrails, then forwards the request to the appropriate model — which may be hosted on AWS Bedrock. For Claude Code, AI-VERDE exposes a Bedrock-compatible endpoint at /bedrock, so Claude Code can use its built-in Bedrock support while AI-VERDE handles authentication and budgets. Other clients should use AI-VERDE's OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-style endpoints instead; see Base URL and Authentication.

Note

The Bedrock-style endpoint is only intended for Claude Code. To call Claude models from your own code, use the Anthropic Python SDK, which uses the Anthropic-style API.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Using Anthropic Python SDK with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Anthropic Python SDK is Anthropic's official Python SDK for interacting with Claude models. AI-VERDE can serve as the backend for the Anthropic Python SDK, routing requests through AI-VERDE's budget controls and guardrails to the Claude models available to your course or team.

Note

The Anthropic Python SDK uses AI-VERDE's Anthropic-style API at https://llm-api.cyverse.ai. It does not use the /bedrock endpoint, which is reserved for Claude Code, even when your Claude models are hosted on AWS Bedrock.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key and note the AI-VERDE base URL. The base URL used in the script must have the /v1 suffix removed, if present. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the Claude model ID you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6 or my-team/claude-sonnet-4-6).
  3. Install Anthropic Python SDK. Instructions can be found at https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Example Python script using Anthropic Python SDK with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Export the following environment variables for your script.

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"

For example:

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-xyz"

Example script:

import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai", # Replace with the AI-VERDE base URL if different
    api_key=os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"),
)

message = client.messages.create(
    max_tokens=128,
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Hello, Claude",
        }
    ],

    model="<model name>", # Replace with a Claude model name from your model list
)

print(message.content)

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic Base URL, strip the /v1 suffix if present.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Using Claude Code with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Claude Code is Anthropic's official CLI coding assistant. AI-VERDE can serve as the backend for Claude Code, routing requests through AI-VERDE's budget controls and guardrails to Anthropic Claude models hosted on AWS Bedrock.

Note

Unlike the non-Bedrock Claude Code setup, which uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the Bedrock setup must put your AI-VERDE API key in ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. When talking to a Bedrock endpoint, Claude Code only sends ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY would be ignored.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key and note the AI-VERDE base URL. The base URL used in the environment variables ends in /bedrock rather than /v1. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the Claude model ID for Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6 or my-team/claude-sonnet-4-6).
  3. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  4. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal with Claude Code installed on Linux or macOS.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 1. Configure Claude Code
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Option 1: ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended)
items.text:
Add the following env section to ~/.claude/settings.json (create the file if it does not exist). Settings in this file apply every time you run Claude Code, in any terminal.

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>",
    "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<model name for opus>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<model name for sonnet>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<model name for haiku>"
  }
}

For example:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "my-team-claude-opus-4-6",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"
  }
}

If the file already has other settings, add the env section alongside them rather than replacing the file.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Option 2: Shell environment variables
items.text:
Alternatively, export the same variables in your terminal before launching Claude Code:

export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL=https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock
export CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH=1
export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="<model name for opus>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="<model name for sonnet>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="<model name for haiku>"

Exported variables only last for the current terminal session. To avoid re-entering them each session, add the lines to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Bedrock Base URL, simply substitute /v1 with /bedrock, e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 to https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock. If both ~/.claude/settings.json and your shell set the same variable, the value in ~/.claude/settings.json is used.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 2. Launch Claude Code
items.text:
Start Claude Code:

claude

You can run /status inside Claude Code to confirm it is using Amazon Bedrock with the AI-VERDE base URL.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: If you need to change your API Key
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your VERDE API Key, update ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN wherever you set it in step 1 (~/.claude/settings.json or your shell profile), then restart Claude Code.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Using VSCode Claude Code Extension with AI-VERDE
items.text: VSCode Claude Code Extension is an official extension from Anthropic for using Claude Code within VSCode. AI-VERDE can serve as the backend for the extension, routing requests through AI-VERDE's budget controls and guardrails to Anthropic Claude models hosted on AWS Bedrock.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key and note the AI-VERDE base URL. The base URL used in the environment variables ends in /bedrock rather than /v1. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the Claude model ID for Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6 or my-team/claude-sonnet-4-6).
  3. Install VS Code. Instructions can be found at https://code.visualstudio.com/download.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 1. Install the "Claude Code for VS Code" extension from Anthropic
items.text: Within the extension marketplace, a simple search for "Claude Code" yields the desired extension.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 2. Configuring "Claude Code for VS Code" extension
items.text:
Go to the extension page.

Click on the gear icon and select "Settings".

Find the setting entry "Claude Code: Disable Login Prompt" and check the box to enable it.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Configuring Environment Variables
items.text:
Next you will need to configure the extension to use AI-VERDE as the backend for Anthropic Claude models hosted on AWS Bedrock. Set these in the extension's own "Claude Code: Environment Variables" setting. The extension checks this setting before launching, so it is the reliable place for your AI-VERDE credentials; values in ~/.claude/settings.json do not reach the extension's login check.

Find the setting entry "Claude Code: Environment Variables" and click on "Edit in settings.json".

You will need to add the following environment variables to the claudeCode.environmentVariables section of the settings:

  • add your AI-VERDE API key as the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
  • add your Bedrock base URL as ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL
  • replace the model IDs with your own team model IDs for Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku
    "claudeCode.environmentVariables": [
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "value": "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_API_KEY"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL", "value":"REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_BEDROCK_BASE_URL"},
        { "name": "CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH", "value":"1"},
        { "name": "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK", "value":"1"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL", "value":"my-team-claude-opus-4-6"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL", "value":"my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL", "value":"my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"}
    ],

For example, with the values filled in:

    "claudeCode.environmentVariables": [
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "value": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL", "value":"https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock"},
        { "name": "CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH", "value":"1"},
        { "name": "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK", "value":"1"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL", "value":"my-team-claude-opus-4-6"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL", "value":"my-team-claude-sonnet-4-6"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL", "value":"my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"}
    ],

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Bedrock Base URL, simply substitute /v1 with /bedrock, e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 to https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock.

Note

This setting only applies to the VS Code extension. To use Claude Code in the terminal as well, configure it separately as described in Using Claude Code.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 3. Restart VS Code
items.text: You may need to restart VS Code for the environment variables & settings to take effect.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

The extension has chat functionality accessed from the leftmost bar in VS Code:

You can also open a chat window by clicking on the Claude logo:

items.title: Chatbox AI
items.text: Chatbox AI is a desktop application that works on Windows, MacOS, Android, iOS, Web, and Linux. These instructions should apply for both Windows and MacOS versions with some variations between the two platforms.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API Key and API URL. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model(s) you want to configure for Chatbox AI. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Install Chatbox AI by visiting this page: https://chatboxai.app/en#download.
  4. The remaining instructions assume you have Chatbox AI installed.

items.title: 1. Configure AI-VERDE in Chatbox AI
items.text:
For these steps, you can refer to the screenshots below.

  1. Launch Chatbox AI.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Model Provider.
  4. Click the "+ Add" button.
  5. Enter "ai-verde" in the Name field.
  6. Leave API Mode set to "OpenAI API Compatible".
  7. Click the Add button. You should then be shown the ai-verde configuration panel on the right.
  8. Enter (or paste) your AI-VERDE Key in the API Key field.
  9. Enter (or paste) the AI-VERDE API URL in the API Host field.
  10. In the model section, click the "New" button, and a new model dialog box will be shown.
  11. Enter the model in the "Model ID" field.

  12. Under capabilities, select the capabilities you know the model supports: vision, reasoning, or tool use.

    Note

    Capabilities for a model can be modified at a later time.

    1. Click on the "Save" button
    2. You can repeat steps 10-13 to add additional models.
    3. Optionally, after adding one or more models, you can click the "Check" button to test the connection to AI-VERDE.

Now you're ready to begin chatting!

items.title: 2. Using Chatbox AI with configured models
items.text:
1. At any time, you can click the "New Chat" button or click a previous conversation in the left panel.
  2. Select the model for this chat session, if necessary.
  3. Enter your request in the chat textbox to begin chatting with the model.

There is a lot of functionality provided by Chatbox AI (as with many other chat interfaces). Feel free to explore!

items.title: Claude Code Router (using non-Anthropic Models)
items.text: You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API Key after installing Claude Code and Claude Code Router. More information on installing and using Claude Code Router can be found here, https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API Key. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key.
  2. Note the model(s) you want to configure for Claude Code. See Getting a List of Models.
  3. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  4. Install Claude Code Router. Instructions can be found here, https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router.
  5. The remaining instructions assume you have an open terminal on a system with Claude Code and bash installed.

items.title: 1. Starting Claude Code Router
items.text:
This step should only be needed the first time you use Claude Code Router.

In a terminal, enter the command ccr start:

ccr start

items.title: 2. Configuring Claude Code Router
items.text:
After running ccr code, you will be prompted to enter the minimum configuration to start Claude Code Router. Use the following table for guidance on the values:

Field Value or Instructions Notes Provider Name ai-verde any string works Provider API KEY enter your AI-VERDE API key Provider URL https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/chat/completions MODEL Name <verde model name> replace <verde model name> with the model you'd like to use

After entering the MODEL name, you should see text similar to the following:

Loaded JSON config from: /root/.claude-code-router/config.json
register transformer: Anthropic (endpoint: /v1/messages)
register transformer: gemini (endpoint: /v1beta/models/:modelAndAction)
register transformer: deepseek (no endpoint)
register transformer: tooluse (no endpoint)
register transformer: openrouter (no endpoint)
register transformer: maxtoken (no endpoint)
providerConfig:  ai-verde undefined
ai-verde provider registered
🚀 LLMs API server listening on http://127.0.0.1:3456
Press ctrl-c so that you can run Claude Code with Claude Code Router.

items.title: 3. Running Claude Code Router
items.text:
Run Claude Code with Claude Code Router using the following command:

ccr code

If you are successful entering Claude Code, congratulations! To use Claude Code with the same settings, you will need to run ccr code every time.

items.title: Updating Claude Code Router configuration
items.text: At some point, you may want to add other models or add or update configuration options. To do so, you can edit the configuration file found in ~/.claude-code-router/config.json.

items.title: Getting Started with OpenAI for Instructors
items.text:
Welcome! If you are new to AI-VERDE, this guide will walk you through the essential first steps to get up and running.

Before you begin: please schedule an onboarding session with an AI-VERDE team coordinator.
path: Getting Started with OpenAI for Instructors

items.title: 1. Obtain an OpenAI Key
items.text:
1. Log in to your OpenAI account.
  2. Click Create new secret key to generate a new key.
  3. Copy the key and store it in a secure location.
path: Getting Started with OpenAI for Instructors

items.title: 2. Create a Stache Entry to Share the OpenAI API Key
items.text:
1. Log in to stache.arizona.edu.
  2. Create a new Stache entry with the OpenAI API key.
  3. Share the entry with all of the following individuals:
  4. edwins@arizona.edu
  5. iychoi@arizona.edu
  6. zhxu73@arizona.edu
path: Getting Started with OpenAI for Instructors

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Having trouble getting started? Here are the most common issues instructors face:

  • Can’t find the API key after creating it → OpenAI only shows the key once. If you lost it, go back to the API Keys page and create a new one.

  • Stache entry not accessible to the AI-VERDE team → Double-check that you shared the entry with all required addresses.
path: Getting Started with OpenAI for Instructors

items.title: Next Step: Gather Your Course Details
items.text: Great work so far! Once your OpenAI key is shared, you’re ready to move on to the next stage: Creating a course by email, then adding your roster (students, TAs, and co-instructors) yourself or by emailing it to support.
path: Getting Started with OpenAI for Instructors

items.title: Request a Course or Team
items.text: To start the process to create a course or team in AI-VERDE, please send an email to ai-verde-support@cyverse.org. There is no form to fill out; course and team setup is handled by email.

items.title: What Happens Next
items.text:
Once you send your request:

  • CyVerse staff will create your course/team in AI-VERDE.
  • After your course/team is created, it will appear in the AI-VERDE dashboard.
  • CyVerse staff will contact you and the owner (if different) after the course/team is created.

items.title: Adding Your Roster
items.text:
Once your course/team is created, you can add your students, TAs, and co-instructors in either of two ways:

  • Add them yourself in the Members tab of your course. See Managing a Course.
  • Email your roster to ai-verde-support@cyverse.org and CyVerse staff will add the members for you.

items.title: Contact and Feedback
items.text: If you are happy with AI-VERDE, we’d love your feedback! Please send comments or critiques to: ai-verde-support@cyverse.org

items.title: Managing a Course in AI-VERDE
items.text: Once your course has been created, you’ll find it listed in your AI-VERDE dashboard. From here, owners and instructors can update course details, manage members, monitor usage, and design AI-powered learning activities.

items.title: Course Overview
items.text:
The Overview tab is your course’s home base. Here, you can:

  • Change the course name and description
  • Update the title to match your course.
  • Add a clear description so students know the purpose.
  • Set start and end dates
  • Determines when the course appears on members’ dashboards.
  • Example: If you set a start date for Sept 1, the course will not appear on students’ dashboards before that date. Students can still sign in to AI-VERDE, but they will not see the course.
  • After the end date, the course no longer appears on members’ dashboards.
  • Adjust course activity status
  • Switch a course to Active when ready for students.
  • Change to Inactive if you want to temporarily hide the course from members’ dashboards without deleting it.

A course appears on members’ dashboards only while it is Active and the current date is between its start and end dates.

items.title: Managing Members
items.text:
The Members tab gives you full control over who is enrolled and what they can do.

Features:

  • Add new members
  • Enter the user’s email address.
  • Assign them a role at the time of adding.
  • Remove members
  • Select a user and remove them from the course.
  • Useful if a student drops the class or a TA changes.
  • Edit member roles
  • Roles determine what access each user has (see below).

items.title: Roles
items.text:
Each course has one Owner and may have any number of Co-owners, in addition to members with the Instructor, TA, or Student role.

Action Owner / Co-owner Instructor TA Student Edit course name, description, dates, and status ✓ ✓ Add and remove members ✓ ✓ ✓ Change a member’s role ✓ ✓ View course and individual usage ✓ ✓ ✓ Create, edit, and delete prompts ✓ ✓ ✓ Use the course chat and course prompts ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Get a personal API key ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓

Tip: If a student says they can’t see the course, check the Members tab first to make sure they are listed.

items.title: Budget and Usage
items.text:
AI-VERDE resources are tied to a budget, managed in coordination with the CyVerse team.

  • Budgets are set by CyVerse
  • The course budget and any per-student budgets are set by CyVerse staff. To request a change, email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org.
  • What you can do as an owner, instructor, or TA:
  • View individual usage → see how much each student has consumed.
  • View total course usage → monitor whether the class is approaching budget limits.
  • Why it matters:
  • Helps you plan assignments around available resources.
  • Identifies students who may need guidance if their usage is unusually high.

items.title: AI Prompts and Content
items.text:
The Prompts feature lets instructors and TAs design and share structured prompts for AI activities.

How to use it:

  1. Go to the Prompts tab.
  2. Write a prompt (e.g., “Summarize today’s lecture into 5 key points”).
  3. Sharing the prompt is automatic: as soon as it is saved, every member of the course can see it and use it to generate AI responses inside Verde.
  4. Review outputs to ensure alignment with learning goals.

This feature helps standardize assignments and ensures all students are working from the same AI instructions.

items.title: API Keys and Integrations
items.text:
Instructors can extend Verde beyond the platform using API keys.

  • Generate API keys
  • Useful for advanced workflows, automation, or integrating Verde with other systems. See the AI-VERDE API documentation.
  • Why this matters:
  • Keeps Verde flexible, fitting into your department’s existing tools rather than operating as an isolated system.

items.title: Troubleshooting While Managing
items.text:
• Course doesn’t show up? → Confirm with support that your course was created, that its status is Active, and that today is between its start and end dates.
  • A student can’t see the course? → Verify they are listed under Members. If not, add them. Also check the course status and dates.
  • Budget concerns? → Email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org to review or request an adjustment.
  • Prompt not working as expected? → Double-check the prompt’s wording and edit it in the Prompts tab; changes are visible to members immediately.

items.title: Troubleshooting Guide
items.text: This guide covers the most common issues instructors face when getting started, creating a course, and managing a course in AI-VERDE.

items.title: Getting Started Issues
items.text:
• Can’t find the API key after creating it

  • OpenAI only shows the key once. If you lost it, return to the API Keys page and generate a new one.

  • Stache entry not accessible to the AI-VERDE team

  • Double-check you shared the entry with all required addresses:
    • edwins@arizona.edu
    • iychoi@arizona.edu
    • zhxu73@arizona.edu

items.title: Creating a Course Issues
items.text:
• Course request emailed but no response
  • Wait up to 48 hours for processing.

  • Check your spam/junk folder for CyVerse messages.

  • Some students missing from the roster

  • Add them yourself in the Members tab of your course, or

  • Email the missing members to ai-verde-support@cyverse.org.

  • Course details are incorrect (name, description, or term)

  • Owners and instructors can edit the name, description, and dates in the Overview tab.
  • Otherwise, contact ai-verde-support@cyverse.org with the corrections.

items.title: Managing a Course Issues
items.text:
• Course doesn’t show up?
  • Confirm with support that your course was created.

  • Check that the course status is Active and that today is between its start and end dates.

  • A student can’t see the course?

  • Verify they are listed under Members. If not, add them.

  • Check the course status and dates, as above.

  • Budget seems off or not updating

  • Budgets are managed by CyVerse.
  • By default, budgets are monthly and reset on the 1st of each month, so usage drops back to zero at that point. Some courses use a different reset schedule.

  • Instructors can view usage but not set budgets — email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org for adjustments.

  • Students can’t access prompts

  • Prompts are shared with all course members automatically. Check that the prompt still exists in the Prompts tab and was not deleted.

  • Check that the student is listed under Members and can see the course (see above).

  • Error generating API keys

  • Retry after refreshing your dashboard session.

items.title: Support Contact
items.text: If these steps don’t solve your issue, reach out to the CyVerse team: ai-verde-support@cyverse.org
